questions.prompt: A temperature changes by \(15\,\mathrm{C^\circ}\). What is this interval in Fahrenheit degrees?
questions.answer:
For an interval, use only the scale factor:
\[
\Delta T_F=\frac{9}{5}\Delta T_C=\frac{9}{5}(15)=27\,\mathrm{F^\circ}
\]

questions.prompt: A temperature changes by \(27\,\mathrm{F^\circ}\). What is this interval in Celsius degrees?
A sample warms from \(12\,{}^\circ\mathrm{C}\) to \(47\,{}^\circ\mathrm{C}\). Find the initial and final temperatures in Fahrenheit and the temperature change in Fahrenheit degrees.
questions.answer:
Convert each actual temperature:
\[
T_{Fi}=\frac{9}{5}(12)+32=53.6\,{}^\circ\mathrm{F}
\]
\[
T_{Ff}=\frac{9}{5}(47)+32=116.6\,{}^\circ\mathrm{F}
\]
The interval is
\[
\Delta T_F=116.6-53.6=63.0\,\mathrm{F^\circ}
\]
Equivalently, \(\Delta T_C=35\,\mathrm{C^\circ}\), so \((9/5)(35)=63\,\mathrm{F^\circ}\).

questions.prompt: At what temperature do the Celsius and Fahrenheit scales have the same numerical reading?
questions.answer:
Set the numerical readings equal: \(T_F=T_C=T\).
\[
T=\frac{9}{5}T+32
\]
\[
-\frac{4}{5}T=32
\]
\[
T=-40
\]
So the scales agree numerically at
\[
-40\,{}^\circ\mathrm{C}=-40\,{}^\circ\mathrm{F}
\]

questions.prompt: A thermometer scale \(X\) is linear. It reads \(10\,{}^\circ\mathrm{X}\) at \(0\,{}^\circ\mathrm{C}\) and \(90\,{}^\circ\mathrm{X}\) at \(100\,{}^\circ\mathrm{C}\). Derive \(T_X\) in terms of \(T_C\).
A weather report says the temperature rose from \(41\,{}^\circ\mathrm{F}\) to \(59\,{}^\circ\mathrm{F}\). Find the temperature change in Celsius degrees and the final temperature in Celsius.
questions.answer:
The Fahrenheit interval is
\[
\Delta T_F=59-41=18\,\mathrm{F^\circ}
\]
so
\[
\Delta T_C=\frac{5}{9}(18)=10\,\mathrm{C^\circ}
\]
The final actual temperature is
\[
T_C=\frac{5}{9}(59-32)=15\,{}^\circ\mathrm{C}
\]

questions.prompt: A proposed scale \(Y\) has equal degree size to the Celsius scale but reads \(125\,{}^\circ\mathrm{Y}\) at \(100\,{}^\circ\mathrm{C}\). Derive the conversion between \(Y\) and Celsius, then find the \(Y\) reading at \(-40\,{}^\circ\mathrm{C}\).
questions.answer:
Equal degree size means the conversion has slope \(1\):
\[
T_Y=T_C+b
\]
At \(100\,{}^\circ\mathrm{C}\), the reading is \(125\,{}^\circ\mathrm{Y}\), so
\[
125=100+b\Rightarrow b=25
\]
Thus
\[
T_Y=T_C+25
\]
At \(-40\,{}^\circ\mathrm{C}\):
\[
T_Y=-40+25=-15\,{}^\circ\mathrm{Y}
\]
